summary.signal: Engineering agents are moving into production engineering workflows where parity checks, certified/signoff flows, and explicit validation gates matter more than raw generation alone.

Scientific and engineering ML is shifting toward interpretable or property-grounded models: local neural operators and atomistic foundation models are being judged against physical observables and numerical structure.

Industrial AI deployment is becoming infrastructure-specific: on-premises semiconductor AI, edge AI for aerospace/defense, and Physical AI for heavy equipment impose data-residency, latency, reliability, and safety constraints.
Agent governance is becoming an execution-layer problem with evaluation, tool-call policy, scoped credentials, destructive-action gates, and network-egress controls.
Enterprise survey evidence points to orchestration, data readiness, workflow integration, and governance as scaling constraints; vendor-survey selection effects remain material.

central_signals: Verification infrastructure is becoming the core engineering requirement for agentic execution.
Physics-aware validation is more informative than generic ML accuracy for Scientific AI deployment.
Industrial AI deployment choices are being constrained by data locality, edge compute, operational safety and system reliability.
Agent governance is moving from policy documents into pre-execution controls, evaluation and observability.
tensions_or_caveats: Cadence, Mistral, Samsung, EdgeCortix, Red Hat and Backblaze evidence is first-party; performance and productivity claims must remain attributed.
LGNO is an arXiv preprint and should not be presented as peer-reviewed evidence.
UiPath is a vendor-authored self-reported survey; the 89% ROI figure is conditional on an already mature orchestration subgroup and does not establish causality.
The Reuters incident follow-up is independent reporting, but site-count estimates vary across investigators and are incomplete.
The Company Scout recovered several August MSC items that were newly discovered rather than newly published; they remain backlog rather than headline candidates.

known_gaps: Today's Company Scout rotation is CAD/CAE-heavy and contains no current aircraft-engine OEM watch item.
No strong net-new frontier/open-weight model release survived recent-handoff deduplication; the model lane was not padded.

Several enterprise-agent security candidates are vendor product announcements with overlapping themes; only candidates with the clearest execution controls or independent incident evidence were selected.

Research Scout recorded that the same-day Company Scout was unavailable during its own run even though the current Company artifact is timestamped earlier; both artifacts are now present, same-day, complete and fresh, so this is treated as a non-blocking repository-visibility/race warning.
